brief: One week combined a hotter-than-expected CPI (third straight miss), an unresolved Iran blockade, a midterm result seen as hostile to data centers, and Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO. Goldman's cross-asset scorecard shows the dollar and safe havens as this week's winners, with CCC high yield and front-end Treasury futures the worst losers. On AI infrastructure, Goldman argues the post-midterm world rewards hyperscalers that already control power and compute capacity over neocloud tenants dependent on leases, even as hyperscaler IG credit spreads widened toward 163bp and CoreWeave's CDS more than doubled since May while non-IG AI debt issuance stopped entirely. Goldman also ties the AI equity rally to consumption: a 30%/15% downside scenario would turn a roughly 0.4pp wealth-effect tailwind into a 0.6pp drag on 2027 growth. On Nvidia, Goldman's first take likens Jensen's exit to Jobs' 2011 absence, expects a similar multiple de-rating, but still calls the stock buyable given ~80% expected EPS growth, with Nov 17 earnings the first test under interim CEO Colette Kress. Because Iran risk and a possible Dec 11 shutdown fight keep energy prices from fully offsetting CPI, Goldman adds a third 25bp hike for March 2027 while leaving its terminal rate unchanged, below where markets price out to 2028.
